investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-30T00:50–00:57Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported Insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained unscheduled for ~145–148 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node in the 6-node cluster could accept a new remote-agent pod at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never received a vmId or remoteState value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent from the check result.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning the schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size. If the selector is too narrow, capacity will be exhausted more quickly.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user sessions may have left pods running that were not cleaned up, reducing available capacity for new probe pods.
Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been provisioned with a resource limit that is too low for concurrent eval and production workloads.
